newsitem.title: USA: PJM pricing arguments heard at US FERC conference.
newsitem.headline: PJM pricing arguments heard at US FERC conference.

text.p: Members of the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool Friday gave arguments for two different schemes to set charges during periods of high energy demand.

In a technical conference for Federal Energy Regulatory Commission staff, PECO Energy Co, backed by a coalition of other power marketers, argued that congestion charges be incorporated into a single fee for all PJM pool users.
But other pool members that are utilities, banded together as the Supporting Companies Group, argued that users should pay congestions fees based on particular transmission paths.
The utilities said their scheme for locational marginal cost pricing (LMP) reflects that the fact that a single constraint produces different prices at various points on the system.

William Hogan, a consultant to the utilities, said the point-specific pricing gives economic incentives to find proper pricing levels, and helps mitigate market power by avoiding price averages, which he said would be more easily manipulated.

But Eric Van Der Walde, vice president of Eastern U.S. Power Trading for Enron Power Marketing, said the Supporting Companies Group plan in effect would rebundle transmission and generation services and create "opaque" pricing. He called the scheme an over-reaction to a relatively minor problem of congestion at known points.
"LMP is a poor vehicle for maximizing fairness and openess goals," Van Der Walde, representing the Coalition for a Competitive Electric Market (CCEM), said.
The Supporting Companies' plan would use a system of debits, known as Fixed Transmission Rights (FTRs) to return excess collections that would come with their plan.
The utilities said they expected that those would be traded in a secondary market, but PECO and CCEM said the credits would be "point-specific" and would not be traded easily.

The Supporting Companies Group is comprised of seven Mid-Atlantic utilities originally in the pool. Membership in the pool has grown to 22 companies, including a number of power marketers, a spokesman said.
Until the FERC makes a decision in the issue, the pool has operated under PECO's congestion rate plan.
